utterances.text: Mr. President, we were planning Tomo Alilovic for today, but he did not turn up. So we have no more witnesses for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. So we will adjourn, but before doing so, let me suggest -- I assume you will call the accused as witnesses at the end. Now, as you know, we will resume our proceedings on the 3rd of May, first of all with the three court witnesses and then with the witnesses to be called by Counsel Krajina. Since Counsel Krajina intends to start with the president of the Supreme Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I believe that's what you said. However, having read again the two judgements he is expected to comment on, I wonder to what extent we really need his testimony. It depends on what you intend to ask him because I honestly think those two judgements are hardly of any relevance to us. I hope you are not going to ask him questions about his notion of persecution or the notion of persecution laid down in the case law of Bosnia-Herzegovina because we are not particularly interested in that notion. We will have to apply the notion of persecution as it is laid down in our Statute and in public International Law. So could you please explain to us once again on what particular points do you intend to call the President of the Supreme Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina in May?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJINA
utterances.text: Mr. President, we already gave an explanation at the outset when we moved to that effect, and we also indicated why we believed that his testimony would be useful in these proceedings. On the basis of that motion, which was accompanied by the reasons for it, and as far as I know, the Trial Chamber approved the summoning of this witness and his testimony before the court. I may add that we simply wanted to indicate what is the judicial practice in Bosnia-Herzegovina with regard to the crime of persecution of civilian population in time of war, and because there were such cases in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the precedent of the Supreme Court does have inclination, naturally, what is the judicial practice, what kind of facts are required, what kind of elements are required to define the persecution of civilian population and, therefore, on which basis may people be charged with the persecution of the civilian population, and which are the sanctions envisaged by the Criminal Code of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We also believe that this kind of information would be useful to this Tribunal because we think that the elements required to qualify something as a crime and has possibility for the kind of crime in that country whose nationals are charged with them, we thought that it would be useful if the court had this information so as to clarify problems which exist both de facto and in jure with the problem, the problem -- I mean, persecution of the civilian population, the qualification of this crime, and the responsibility for this crime. In a nutshell, that is what we thought should be material to this case. I do not think that the testimony would take too much time, and we think that it will be very useful. Thank you very much. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right, Counsel Krajina, yes, the President of the Supreme Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina will be allowed to give evidence in court, only on the judicial practice of courts in Bosnia-Herzegovina concerning persecution, but this evidence should be given briefly, in a concise way, and then it will be for us to decide what relevance, if any, to give to this evidence, because, as you know, in principle, we have to apply only our Statute and international law, customary and treaty law. We are duty-bound to look into the judicial practice of the former Yugoslavia only as far as sentencing is concerned, under Article 24(1) of our Statute. So I very much hope that you will stick to these guidelines when the President of the Supreme Court will be called here. Are there any other matters to be discussed before we adjourn until the 3rd of May? The Prosecutor has nothing? No? The Defence? I hope that the Defence counsel will hand in a list of witnesses for the 3rd of May, to be called as from the 3rd of May, by, say, the 26th of April, I wonder, if you don't mind, so that we have a few days to prepare. The Defence counsel will then provide the Prosecutor and the Court with this list around the 26th of April. We will resume our proceedings on the 3rd of May at 9.00, and we will follow the usual schedule, from 9.00 to 1.30. So we adjourn the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: 11.23 a.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of May, 1999, at 9.00 a.m.
